summary: Osamu Hayashima works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and researched at the University of Hamburg in 1992. He held posts at Nagasaki University (attested 1979–2003), Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2003–2013), and Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2015).
Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Takata was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as head of the art department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

Osborn Bergin was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning under Kuno Meyer, and the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940).

Oskar von Hinüber is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Tübingen, Erlangen-Nürnberg, and Mainz, where he earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme and completed his habilitation. He directed the Nepal Research Centre (~1975–1977) and was a professor at Freiburg (1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi specializes in archaeology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, the CNRS, and the Sorbonne under Paul Bernard and Jean-Marie Dentzer. He was an emeritus director at the CNRS (1989) and adjunct professor at UC Berkeley (~2014).

Osvald Sirén was an art historian and sinologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Helsinki. He held a professorship at Stockholm University (1908–1923), worked as a conservator at Musée Guimet (1924–1925), and served as keeper at the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

Othmar Frank was an Indologist who studied in Paris and London. He taught at Banz Abbey School, the Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and the University of Bamberg, before holding professorships at the University of Würzburg (from 1821) and the University of Munich (from 1826).
Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji from ~1927 to 1930. He later served as a professor at Chuo University from ~1958 to 1974.

Otto Blau was a scholar of Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle, Leipzig University, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, studying under August Friedrich Pott between ~1848 and 1852.

Otto Fischer was an art historian who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920), head of the Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and associate professor of art history at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a sinologist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the chair of Chinese Language and Culture at the University of Hamburg and Hamburg Colonial Institute (1910–1923) and was professor of sinology at Humboldt University (1923–1931).

Otto Höfler was an Austrian linguist and religious studies scholar who studied at Vienna under Rudolf Much, Lund, and Kiel. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and the University of Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn was an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Kiel University (~1839–1845), the University of Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig University (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen was an archaeologist, sinologist, and Central Asian specialist. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, later working at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (1927–1929), Mills College (1939–1947), and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Neugebauer was an Austrian-American historian of mathematics and science who studied at Graz, Munich, and Göttingen under Boris Turayev. He held professorships at Copenhagen (1933–1939) and Brown University (1939, 1947–1969), and was a permanent member at the Institute for Advanced Study (1980–1990).

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Sergey Oldenburg, as well as in Bonn and under Rudolf Lange. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University in Prague, completing his doctorate under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. In 1929, he became a member of the research section at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences.

Otto Strauss was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel University (1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served as a member and director at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and taught at the University of Jena (~1868–1885).
